next_steps: Request the original surveillance video from both restaurants and any neighboring businesses, in native format with the system clock offset. Ask for the full approach, ramming and departure sequence. Check retention first, since the August video may already be overwritten. If it was exported, get that copy from the department's evidence system.

Extract from the video the Jeep's make, model, generation, color, wheels, damage, plate if visible, and the direction of travel. Compare the two Jeeps side by side. Ask video forensics to enhance the footage and the NEW-048 photograph.

Pull stolen-vehicle reports for black Jeeps in King County and neighboring jurisdictions. Search the window from a few days before each incident (2023-08-08 and 2023-09-13) through the incident date. Match the theft location, time and method (key, relay, tow) and look for the same pattern in both.

Run the stolen-vehicle plates and VINs through license plate reader (ALPR) hits, recovery records and impound or tow logs, to find where each Jeep ended up and whether it was recovered. Request a forensic exam of any recovered Jeep: prints, DNA, tools, items left inside.

Re-interview the witnesses listed in both reports, or retrieve the full statements. Ask about the number of people, descriptions, direction of flight, a second vehicle, and what was said or heard. Record contact details and a role for each.

Canvass both blocks for additional cameras (doorbells, traffic and transit cameras, nearby businesses) covering the approach and escape routes. Do it for the hours around each incident, using the time the restaurant alarm or the 911 call recorded.
Pull the 911/CAD logs and alarm-company records for both incidents to fix the incident time, the first responders and any callers. Get the first officers' body-worn camera video of the scene.

Ask each restaurant owner what was taken or damaged (cash, safe, register, stock) and what else was touched, and whether either has an insurance or loss claim. Check whether the owners or staff share a vendor, supplier, former employee or other tie.

Collect scene evidence if it has not been done: glass and paint transfer, vehicle debris and any tool marks. Request lab comparison between the two scenes. For the NEW-048 scene, check if any evidence was kept at all.

Query regional and state records (RMS, NIBRS and regional crime-analysis bulletins) for other ram-raid or vehicle-through-storefront burglaries, in Renton and nearby cities, around those dates. This tests whether the pattern is local to these two or part of a wider series.
Do not rely on this link as more than a moderate lead until the Jeep identity or video comparison supports or rules out a shared vehicle.

props.rationale: Both are residential burglaries in New Canaan, CT, in October 2025 (day unknown for each). Both report entry through the second floor, which is an uncommon method. Both took jewelry, and both reported high losses (66,400 dollars and 88,000 dollars). The streets differ (Ferris Hill Road and Rosebrook Road). Neither report gives exact dates, times, points of entry, vehicles or footage. The link is therefore tentative and rests on method, item, place and month overlap only.

reasons: Specific shared facts: only entry through the second floor is a candidate rare method. Both reports record it only in the free-text 'Other' field. Neither gives a point of entry, damage or how the second floor was reached, so the method is a loose match.
Same city and the same month (October 2025) are generic. The day is unknown for both, so the incidents could be weeks apart. This does not meet the 'within a few days' fact.

Both cases are listed under the Oenoke Ridge neighborhood, but the narratives never state a neighborhood (NEW-035 lists 'Neighborhood within New Canaan' as unknown). The streets differ (Ferris Hill Road and Rosebrook Road), so the neighborhood match is weakly supported.

Item overlap is jewelry, which is a common category with no distinctive detail. NEW-035 also lists watches. NEW-036 lists foreign currency, handbags and about 20 ounces of gold. The high loss values (66,400 and 88,000 dollars) are unverified totals and not a distinctive match.

No vehicle, footage, plate or suspect information is reported in either case, so nothing ties the two incidents beyond a shared pattern. Nothing contradicts the link: same town, same month, compatible methods.
At most one fairly specific fact (second-floor entry) is supported, and it is thinly documented. That makes the link weak. It is a plausible lead and not a refuted one.
would_change_mind: Exact dates showing the incidents fall within a few days of each other.
Confirmation that both offenders reached the second floor the same way (ladder, balcony or a particular window), or matching damage.
A vehicle, plate, camera footage or witness description common to both scenes.
Itemized loss lists showing distinctive matching items, such as particular watch brands or gold in a similar form.
Verification that the two addresses are in the same neighborhood.
Other New Canaan second-floor burglaries in the same period that show how common this entry method is locally. A very common method would push the verdict lower. A rare one would push it higher.

entries.message: Agrees with public record: 4 of 4 proposed series

missing: Footage content: no report says whether the video was reviewed, retained or recovered, or what it shows (suspect count, clothing, build, vehicle, tools, entry method) for NEW-014, 015, 016 and 017.
Suspect details: no description or count is recorded. NEW-017 mentions a single suspect, and the other three give no count. Nothing yet shows the same actor or group.
Vehicle: reported as not reported or not stated in all four cases, so there is no make, plate or direction of travel.

Entry method and tool: 'broke in through the front door' is not described further. It is unknown whether the door was forced, pried, smashed or left unlocked, and no tool is named. Damage is not reported in NEW-014, 016 or 017.
Property loss: every report says only 'cash and/or electronic devices', with no itemization, serial numbers, amounts or values. It is not known whether cash, electronics or both were taken.

Business type and exact address: only the block is known (2100 E 4th St, 2800 E PCH, 2200 Lakewood Blvd, 5600 E PCH), with no business type. It is unknown whether the targets share a type, such as the same sector or chain.
Alarm and access data: no alarm activation, response time, keyholder or door and lock records are recorded.
Exact times: all four times are approximate (06:08, 06:30, 05:45, 03:20). Exact entry and exit times are not established, so the sequence and any overlap between scenes cannot be checked.
Physical and forensic evidence: 'other evidence' is not reported. No prints, DNA, tool marks, shoe impressions or trace evidence is recorded.
Witnesses and reporting parties: no witnesses are identified, and the reporting party's role (owner or employee) and how the loss was discovered are not stated.
Follow-up status: no arrests, recovered property, pawn or resale hits, or investigator notes are recorded.

Link strength: the cited similarities (forced front door, cash or electronics, early morning, Long Beach) are common and templated, so no distinguishing signature is shown. Confidence is 0.5, and nearby unlinked burglaries are not ruled out.
next_steps: Footage: request and preserve the video for all four scenes now, before overwrite. Get native-format exports with the DVR clock offset noted. Review them for suspect count, clothing, gait, tools, entry technique and vehicle. Compare across scenes for matching clothing, build or behavior.

Neighborhood cameras: canvass adjacent businesses, transit stops, traffic cameras and city or business-district cameras along E 4th St, E PCH and Lakewood Blvd for the 03:00 to 06:45 windows. Look for a vehicle or on-foot route that appears near more than one scene.
ALPR and vehicle data: request plate-reader hits near each scene during the entry windows, and look for vehicles that repeat across scenes.
Alarm and access records: get alarm company logs, door-sensor events and keyholder call records. They give exact entry and exit times and show whether the front door was forced.

Re-contact reporting parties: get itemized loss lists with amounts, serial numbers, IMEIs and account identifiers. Confirm business type, how the door was secured, and whether the door was forced or unlocked. Ask about recent employee, contractor or delivery access, and about earlier incidents.

Scene reprocessing: check the front doors and frames for tool marks, and photograph and cast any impressions. Collect prints and DNA from the door, cash area and handled items. Submit lab requests for latent prints, DNA and tool-mark comparison, and compare tool marks across scenes.
Property tracing: enter serial-numbered electronics in stolen-property databases. Check pawn, secondhand and online-marketplace records, and use device-locator data where available.

Canvass: do an early-morning canvass of each block for witnesses, such as people on the street at the time of the burglaries, delivery drivers and overnight workers. Ask about sounds of glass breaking or about vehicles seen.

Records and pattern check: query RMS and CAD for other commercial burglaries by forced front door in Long Beach and neighboring areas, before and after 2023-02-03 to 2023-02-11. Review the 2023-05-24 case (NEW-018) only for a distinguishing detail, and check whether the four cases share a modus operandi beyond what the templated reports show.

Strengthen or drop the link: record a clear entry-method, tool and suspect-behavior comparison from the footage and scene evidence. If nothing distinguishing emerges, keep the hypothesis at low confidence and don't use it to support a suspect lead.

props.rationale: Three commercial-premises break-ins in New Orleans within 5 days (2023-07-22, 07-26, 07-27). All three involved forced entry and all three reports record the same white Nissan Xterra SUV. The vehicle is the most specific link. Limits: forced entry is a common method. None of the reports says how the SUV relates to the incident. No items are reported taken, and NEW-040 and NEW-041 are classed as attempts. The sites are on different blocks (1600 S Gayoso, 300 N Carrollton, 3600 Prytania), and the reports give no time of day, suspect description or footage. This is a lead for investigators to check, not a confirmed series.

reasons: Shared vehicle: all three case records (NEW-040, NEW-041, NEW-042) record the same white Nissan Xterra SUV, described by color, make and body style. Under the rubric a vehicle seen in the case records counts as a specific shared fact even though no report says how it relates to the incident.
Temporal proximity: the incidents fall on 2023-07-22, 07-26 and 07-27, all within 5 days. This is a second specific shared fact.
Supporting but generic facts: all three are commercial premises in New Orleans with forced entry. Forced entry is a common method, so these facts do not carry the link by themselves.

Nothing contradicts the link. The cities, scene types and method are compatible, and the dates are close. The different blocks (1600 S Gayoso, 300 N Carrollton, 3600 Prytania) don't contradict it, because no neighborhoods are reported and the sites are in the same city.

Weaknesses to keep in mind: NEW-040 and NEW-041 are classed as attempts and NEW-042 as a burglary, which may be a difference in outcome rather than in method. No items are reported taken. No time of day, footage or suspect description is reported. The Xterra could be an officer's note about a bystander or reporting party's vehicle. This is an investigative lead, not a confirmed series.

No case is an outlier. All three share the vehicle, the time window and the method. NEW-042 differs only in being classed as a completed burglary, and its items-missing field is unreported, not 'none'.
I make no inference about who any suspect is.
would_change_mind: Plates or a VIN for the Xterra showing different vehicles, or showing that the vehicle belongs to a reporting party or to someone with a legitimate reason to be at each site.
Reports clarifying that the Xterra was recorded only as a bystander or unrelated vehicle at one or more scenes.
Footage, tool-mark or entry-method details that differ materially between the three sites.
Times of day, or a suspect description, that conflict between the cases.
Further cases at these addresses or nearby that show the Xterra was a common local vehicle, such as a business vehicle parked in the area.
Confirmation from the reports of what was taken in NEW-042, and whether it differs from the other two in a way that suggests a different actor.

props.rationale: All three are residential burglaries in the same Lower Moreland Township, PA development (Pine Road or Red Lion Road area). Each report records the same entry method, kicking in a rear glass door or forcing open doors. Each report describes that method as used across a series. NEW-032 and NEW-033 are 4 days apart (2023-W28). NEW-034 follows about 60 days later (2023-W36). Limits: the reports attribute the method to the series, not to the specific date. The street is unconfirmed for each date. No items, vehicle, footage or damage are recorded, so the link rests on method, place and scene type only.

reasons: Shared facts are generic. A forced rear door or kicked-in glass door is a common burglary method, not a rare one like vehicle ramming or safe cutting.

All three reports attribute the entry method to the series, not to the specific date. That makes the method an assumption inherited from the grouping, not an independent observation for each incident, so it adds little support.
The neighborhood is not confirmed for any case. Each report says 'Pine Road or Red Lion Road area', and the street is unreported. The shared location is a loose area, not a confirmed match.
The only specific shared fact that holds up is timing. NEW-032 and NEW-033 are 4 days apart (2023-07-11 and 2023-07-15). That is one specific fact, and one alone is weak.

NEW-034 (2023-09-09) is the outlier. It is about 60 days after the other two, with no shared vehicle, item or other distinguishing detail to bridge the gap. The link for NEW-034 rests only on generic method and area.
No items, vehicle, footage, damage or time of day are recorded in any case. Nothing contradicts the link, but nothing specific confirms it either.
The rationale's 0.6 confidence looks high. The rationale itself admits the link rests on method, place and scene type only.
would_change_mind: Confirmed street addresses showing the cases are on the same street or within the same few blocks.
A vehicle description (color and body style or make) recorded at two or more incidents.
Case-specific entry details that are not just the series-wide statement, such as the same door type, tool marks or a distinctive forced-entry pattern at each address.
A matching distinctive item category taken at two or more incidents.
Footage, forensic evidence or a time of day that matches across incidents.
Evidence that places NEW-034 in the series on its own facts, to justify the 60-day gap. Without it, the NEW-032/NEW-033 pair should be judged separately.

entries.message: Agrees with public record: 4 of 4 proposed series

missing: Exact street and address for each of NEW-032, NEW-033 and NEW-034. Only a Pine Road or Red Lion Road area is given, and it is not confirmed per date.
Name of the residential development, and whether all three addresses are in it.
Time of day for each incident. All three have no time, and NEW-034 is only marked approximate.
Whether the entry method (kicking in a rear glass door or forcing open doors) was observed at each specific scene. The reports attribute it to the series, not to the date.
Door and damage details per scene: which door, what force marks, tool marks, glass breakage pattern, and any other damage.
Items taken at each address, and whether anything was recovered. All are recorded as not reported.
Any camera footage: doorbell, home security, neighbor cameras, or township and road cameras. None is recorded.
Any vehicle information: sightings, plates, or vehicles parked or passing near the scenes.
Other physical evidence: prints, DNA, footwear impressions, tool marks. None is recorded.
Witness or neighbor statements, and who discovered each break-in and when. No witness details are recorded.
When each home was last known secure, so the window of occurrence can be narrowed.
Whether the occupants were home or away, and whether there were alarms or alarm activations.
Basis for the 'series' language in the reports: which other incidents belong to the series and how that was determined.
Explanation for the roughly 60-day gap before NEW-034, and whether any similar incidents in that gap went unlinked.
next_steps: Pull the full incident reports 23-096400, 23-078826 and 23-058463 and the responding officers' notes. Confirm the exact address, time found, and entry point at each scene, and check whether the series-wide entry language was copied between reports.
Request CAD and dispatch logs for the three incidents. They give the call time, the caller, the exact address and the units on scene.

Run a canvass of the development around all three addresses. Ask about doorbell and home cameras, unfamiliar vehicles or people, noises, and when residents were away. Collect footage right away, because retention is often short and the 2023 footage may already be gone.
Send footage requests or preservation letters to any camera owners found. Also check township, road and nearby commercial cameras on the Pine Road and Red Lion Road approaches for the three dates.
Check the scene files for photos, and for any prints, DNA, footwear or tool-mark collection. If items were collected, request lab analysis and comparison of tool marks across the three doors.
Contact the victims or recheck the claims for lists of stolen items, serial numbers and alarm records. Enter any serialized items into NCIC and check pawn, resale and online marketplace records.

Query the records system for other burglaries in Lower Moreland and neighboring townships in the gaps and around these dates, to test the series claim and the 60-day gap. Compare method, time of day and target type.
Check for license plate reader hits and traffic stops near the development on the three dates, and field interview cards for the area.
Contact neighboring agencies and any regional burglary or intelligence sharing group to learn whether the same method and area appear in their cases.
Keep the confidence at 0.6 until street-level location, a scene-specific entry method, or physical or video evidence ties the cases together.

Four of the new cases are pre-dawn (about 05:00 to 06:45), like NEW-014 at about 06:08. NEW-067 and NEW-068 fall in the same February 2023 weeks as the anchors (W05/W06, 2 to 6 days apart). NEW-018 and NEW-069 come later, on 2023-05-24 (104 days apart), and NEW-069 is at about 00:41, so they are weaker members. The shared attributes (forced door, cash/electronics, Long Beach, business) are fairly common, so this is moderate confidence. NEW-071 is excluded: it was a daytime walk-in theft of merchandise with a struggle, with no point of entry reported, and its forced-door edge is not supported by the report.

reasons: All four cases share city (New Canaan), month (October 2025, no day), residential target and entry via the second floor. City and month are generic, and with day unknown the cases may be weeks apart, so they don't count as a close-in-time fact.

Second-floor entry is the only distinctive shared fact, and it is thin. Every report lists point of entry and damage as not reported, so we don't know how the second floor was reached (ladder, window, balcony). Only one specific fact remains, which is weak under the rubric.

Jewelry in all four is a broad item category with no distinctive detail such as brand, type or quantity. Watches appear in only two cases (NEW-035, NEW-090) and cash in two others (NEW-036, NEW-089). Handbags, foreign currency and about 20 oz of gold appear only in NEW-036. Homes commonly hold jewelry, so this adds little.
High loss values (38,250 to 88,000 dollars) are unitemized and unverified. Many affluent-area burglaries have similar totals, so this is not a distinctive link.
No vehicle, footage, neighborhood or day is recorded in any case, so no second specific fact can be counted. These gaps are unknowns, not contradictions, and nothing in the data contradicts the link.

Streets differ (Ferris Hill Road, Rosebrook Road, Dan's Highway) and no neighborhood is recorded, so there is no same-neighborhood fact. NEW-089 and NEW-090 share Dan's Highway, which suggests a closer pair, but street alone isn't a neighborhood fact and this doesn't prove the link.
No case is a clear outlier. NEW-036 differs most in loot (gold, handbags, foreign currency), but this is not a contradiction.
The rationale's own 0.55 confidence and 'circumstantial' wording fit this assessment. The link makes no inference about any suspect's identity.

The S-003 anchor case records, to check directly whether the dates and facts match them.
Times of day that fall in a consistent window.

entries.message: Agrees with public record: 7 of 7 proposed series

missing: Address-specific entry method and point of entry for both cases. The ruse is a series-wide statement that both reports say is not specific to these addresses.
Time of day for both incidents. Neither report gives a time, so the pair can't be checked for time-of-day pattern or travel feasibility.
Any suspect description, witness statement or arrest data tied to either address.
Items taken and loss value. Neither case lists anything missing.
Damage and entry force at either scene.
Vehicle information for both cases.
Surveillance or doorbell footage. Both reports say none was reported, which may mean it was never checked.
Findings from the scene examinations. Both reports say an officer began one, but no results are recorded.
Occupancy status at the time of each incident, and whether anyone saw or spoke to a visitor at the door.
Identity of the series the reports refer to, and which other incidents belong to it. Both reports cite it, but the basis for the series is not in the case data.
Exact addresses and neighborhoods. Only the 6800 block of El Salvador St and the 2600 block of Radnor Ave are known, so the distance and geography between the sites are unconfirmed.
next_steps: Pull the full original reports for 24-003636 and 24-069385 and the CAD/dispatch logs. This should give call times, reporting-party details, the narrative and officer notes. It should also show where the series-wide ruse language came from and which incidents the series covers.

Request the scene examination or evidence-technician records for both addresses, including photos, any latent print or DNA collection and the evidence submission logs. If anything was collected, request lab work such as latent comparison, DNA and touch DNA, and compare across the two scenes.

Run a canvass at both blocks. Ask neighbors about door-knockers, salespeople or service workers on or near each date, any vehicle they saw, and any clipboard, uniform, ID badge or claimed company. Re-interview the residents for their own account of a visitor, what was said and what they found missing.

Collect doorbell, home camera and business camera footage for both blocks. Cover the hours around each date, since the times are unknown. Include nearby intersections and transit stops, and request city traffic or license-plate-reader data if available.

Obtain solicitor and door-to-door permit records, utility and contractor service schedules, and delivery company logs for both blocks on 2024-02-22 and 2024-03-05. Check whether any legitimate worker was in the area.
Get each resident's inventory of missing property, with serial numbers, photos and receipts. Check pawn, secondhand and online resale listings for matching items.

Search the department's records for other burglaries in the same series and for similar ruse burglaries in nearby areas. Compare dates, times, blocks, entry points and items, and re-score the link once address-specific facts exist.
Check for any 911, non-emergency or suspicious-person calls near both addresses on or around each date, including calls where someone knocked and left.

props.rationale: Six commercial-premises burglaries in New Orleans between 2023-07-22 and 2023-07-27 (five in week 2023-W30, NEW-040 in W29). Every report records forced entry and the same vehicle, a white Nissan Xterra SUV. The sites are on different streets (South Gayoso, North Carrollton, Prytania, South I-10 Service Road, Arabella, Oak), so this is a city-wide pattern, not a single-location repeat. Caveats: no report says how the vehicle relates to the incident, and "forced door" is a common method. Items taken, footage, time of day and suspect details are unknown in all six. NEW-040 and NEW-041 are recorded as attempted burglaries with nothing taken. The link rests on method, vehicle, target type and a tight time window, so confidence is moderate.

reasons: All six cases are New Orleans commercial premises with forced entry. They fall within 2023-07-22 to 2023-07-27, and five of the six fall within 2023-07-26 to 2023-07-27.

All six records list the same vehicle: a white Nissan Xterra SUV. Under the rubric, a vehicle seen in the case records counts as a shared fact even though no report says how it relates to the incident.
The group shares at least two specific facts: the vehicle, and the tight time window (five incidents within two days). Nothing contradicts them. The facts differ only in generic ways.
Forced entry is a common method and does not count as a specific fact. Each address is block-level only, and none of the six names a neighborhood, so the same-neighborhood fact cannot be counted.

Outliers: NEW-040 (2023-07-22) is four to five days before the rest. It is still within a few days, and it shares the vehicle. NEW-040 and NEW-041 are classed as attempted burglaries with nothing taken, unlike NEW-092, NEW-042, NEW-093 and NEW-094, which are classed as burglaries. This is a difference in outcome, not an incompatible method.
The sites are on different streets across the city. That fits a city-wide pattern, not a single-location repeat, and does not contradict the link.

Caution: a white Nissan Xterra SUV is a fairly common vehicle, and the records may list it as the responding officer's note, a witness vehicle or the premises' vehicle. That could be coincidence or a data-entry artifact, so the evidence supports a link, not a conclusion about who is responsible. No inference about any suspect is drawn or made here.
would_change_mind: A report showing the Xterra belongs to the premises, a responder or an unrelated witness, which would remove it as a shared fact and leave the link weak.
Plates, VIN, or footage showing different Xterras across the sites, or the same vehicle at the sites in a way that confirms the link.
Tool marks or entry details that differ between the cases, such as a pry bar in one and a smashed window in another.
Time of day, items taken or neighborhood data. Matching values would strengthen the link, and clear contradictions would weaken it.
Evidence that the NEW-040 incident on 2023-07-22 is an unrelated event, for example a different report-series pattern, or confirmation that the vehicle field was auto-filled from a template.

entries.message: Agrees with public record: 7 of 7 proposed series

props.rationale: All four are residential burglaries in New Canaan, CT, dated October 2025 (day unknown). Each report records entry through the second floor, which is a less common entry method. Each also lists jewelry among the items taken, and the reported losses are high (38,250 to 88,000 dollars). Watches were taken in NEW-035 and NEW-090. Cash was taken in NEW-036 and NEW-089. The streets differ (Ferris Hill Road, Rosebrook Road, Dan's Highway), so the cases are spread across town. The evidence is circumstantial and the exact dates, times, point of entry, and any footage or vehicle are unknown. The link rests on the shared method, target type, loot pattern, town, and month. It does not identify anyone.

reasons: All four cases share city (New Canaan), month (October 2025, no day), residential target and entry via the second floor. City and month are generic, and with day unknown the cases may be weeks apart, so they don't count as a close-in-time fact.

Second-floor entry is the only distinctive shared fact, and it is thin. Every report lists point of entry and damage as not reported, so we don't know how the second floor was reached (ladder, window, balcony). Only one specific fact remains, which is weak under the rubric.

Jewelry in all four is a broad item category with no distinctive detail such as brand, type or quantity. Watches appear in only two cases (NEW-035, NEW-090) and cash in two others (NEW-036, NEW-089). Handbags, foreign currency and about 20 oz of gold appear only in NEW-036. Homes commonly hold jewelry, so this adds little.
High loss values (38,250 to 88,000 dollars) are unitemized and unverified. Many affluent-area burglaries have similar totals, so this is not a distinctive link.
No vehicle, footage, neighborhood or day is recorded in any case, so no second specific fact can be counted. These gaps are unknowns, not contradictions, and nothing in the data contradicts the link.

Streets differ (Ferris Hill Road, Rosebrook Road, Dan's Highway) and no neighborhood is recorded, so there is no same-neighborhood fact. NEW-089 and NEW-090 share Dan's Highway, which suggests a closer pair, but street alone isn't a neighborhood fact and this doesn't prove the link.
No case is a clear outlier. NEW-036 differs most in loot (gold, handbags, foreign currency), but this is not a contradiction.
The rationale's own 0.55 confidence and 'circumstantial' wording fit this assessment. The link makes no inference about any suspect's identity.
would_change_mind: Exact dates showing the cases fall within a few days of each other (a second specific fact, which would move this toward holds).
A recorded vehicle (color and body style or make) in two or more cases, or camera footage showing one.
Point-of-entry details showing the same method, such as a ladder placed at the same type of window or the same tool marks.
Itemized loot with distinctive matches (the same watch brands, or unusual items such as gold bars) across cases.
A shared neighborhood within New Canaan, or a specific address showing proximity.
Dates or methods showing a case is incompatible, such as months apart or a ground-floor forced entry, which would push toward refuted.

entries.message: Agrees with public record: 6 of 6 proposed series

missing: Time of day for all six incidents (no time recorded in any report), so the 2023-07-22 to 2023-07-27 sequence and any same-night overlap cannot be tested.
Surveillance footage: every report says footage was not reported. It is unknown whether any exists at the six premises or on neighboring properties.
How the white Nissan Xterra SUV relates to each incident (suspect vehicle, witness, premises vehicle, or officer note). No plate, VIN, color shade detail, year or damage is recorded.
Whether the 'light_suv' / white Nissan Xterra in each report is the same vehicle. Six identical descriptions may be a template or shared data entry, not six observations.
Items taken in NEW-042, NEW-092, NEW-093 and NEW-094 (not reported). NEW-040 and NEW-041 list nothing taken, and it is not stated whether a full search of the premises was done.
Forced-entry tool and method detail for all six. 'Forced door' is common, so there are no tool marks, pry points or door type to compare.
Number of perpetrators and any suspect description for all six.
Damage beyond the point of entry, and any other physical evidence (prints, DNA, tool marks, shoe impressions, dropped items). All six say not reported.
Exact addresses. Only block-level locations are given (1600 S Gayoso, 300 N Carrollton, 3600 Prytania, 12000 S I-10 Service Rd, 300 Arabella, 8100 Oak).
Business type, alarm status and discovery time for each premises. Not stated whether alarms triggered, or when each break-in was found compared with when it happened.
Whether NEW-040 (W29, 2023-07-22) belongs to the same series, given it is an attempt, is four days earlier, and has no other tie than the vehicle and method.

Whether the reports were matched to the right incidents. The report numbers are in different ranges (23-006781, 23-011198, 23-057799, 23-074322, 23-093284, 23-098993), which may point to different units or sequences and needs checking.
Any arrests, recoveries or follow-up leads recorded in the full report files.
next_steps: Pull the full incident reports and any supplements for all six report numbers. Check the vehicle field and any officer narrative for plate, source of the vehicle information, and whether it came from a witness or camera.

Canvass for private and business CCTV at each of the six blocks. Prioritize cameras covering the entry door and the street, and request retention before it is overwritten. Many may already be lost given the 2023 dates, so confirm retention status first.
Request city, traffic and LPR camera data covering each block for the incident dates, searched for a white Nissan Xterra. Look for the same vehicle near more than one site.
Query LPR and registration databases for white Nissan Xterras seen near the sites, then compare results across sites. Treat any hit as a lead to verify, not a conclusion.
Ask the reporting parties at each premises for alarm logs, access-control logs, door and lock details, inventory checks and the time the break-in was discovered.
Re-interview the reporting parties and any witnesses about the vehicle: who saw it, where, when, and whether it was tied to people at the scene.

Check whether crime-scene or evidence units processed any of the six. Request photos, tool-mark documentation, and any prints, DNA or trace evidence, and submit lab requests where items were collected. Compare tool marks across doors.
Obtain the dispatch (CAD) logs for each call to get call times, unit arrival and any 'suspect vehicle' notes, and to narrow time of day.
Search for other burglaries in the city and nearby parishes, 2023-07 onward, with forced entry and the same vehicle description, to test whether the pattern is wider or confined to these six.
Check pawn, scrap and resale records if any items are later found to have been taken from NEW-042, NEW-092, NEW-093 or NEW-094.
Decide whether NEW-040 should stay in the group once its details are checked. Keep it separate in notes until a link beyond method and vehicle is found.
